pages.quiz:
PHYSICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

3. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Physics? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Physics.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Physics.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Physics.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Physics.

6. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pressure? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pressure.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pressure.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Pressure.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pressure.

8. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

9. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 100 °C

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mechanical Properties of Materials? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mechanical Properties of Materials.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Mechanical Properties of Materials.

11. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Heating until a solid melts

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Temperature and Thermal Expansion and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Moments and equilibrium and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Energy, Work, Power and Machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Waves and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

2. A — Glucose and oxygen

3. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

4. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Current Electricity Measurement of current, e.m.f., potential difference and res.

5. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Physics.

6. B — Ice melting to water

7. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pressure.

8. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

9. D — 100 °C

10. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mechanical Properties of Materials.

11. A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

12. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Temperature and Thermal Expansion; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Energy, Work, Power and Machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
